title: From zero-section multiplication to the beta-delta chart equation
statement: Fix a finite purity datum P [def-pur-conventions], d,e in N, and a family G of affine-model isomorphisms [def-pur-composition-model-orientation-coordinates]. Suppose its zero-section orientations satisfy b_(d+e) nu_(d,e) = mu(b_d tensor b_e) on every affine finite-type k-base. Suppose also that on every composable affine finite-type smooth pair of ranks d,e, the three beta orientations agree with these b_r in every actual compatible conormal frame. For every such pair f:U->V,g:V->T and every ordinary finite Tate transport t, kappa followed by delta_(gf) and beta_(gf) equals the tensor of delta_f followed by beta_f and the pullback of delta_g followed by beta_g, followed by the specified mu. All maps and normal-coordinate transports are those of [lem-pur-composition-compatible-dnc-charts].

proof.text: On each compatible affine coordinate chart, postcompose the actual DNC pasting identity with b_(d+e). Substitute zero-section multiplication and the three beta identifications, then use functoriality of tensor and pullback. Cover by these charts and descend the resulting equality by detection of automorphisms of the common shifted Tate target. This uses the beta hypothesis on all chart restrictions, not only on one affine smooth pair.
